In this sense, we obtain an almost-robustness result for these cases. I Theorem 7. Let 0 < ε < 1/2, q ∈ (0, 1] and G = (Gn )n∈N be an expander sequence. Let G̃ = (G̃n )n∈N be such that each G̃n is obtained by deleting edges of Gn such that each vertex keeps at least a (1/2 + ε) fraction of its edges. For P ∈ {push, pp} let T̃P denote the number of rounds needed to inform at least n − n/ log n vertices. Then whp (a) T̃push (G̃n ) = log1+q (n) + o(log n). (b) T̃pp (G̃n ) ≤ log1+2q (n) + o(log n), when additionally assuming that δ(Gn ) ≥ αn for some constant 0 < α ≤ 1. We conjecture that there is also a version of Theorem 7b that is true for push&pull on sparse graphs; to be precise we conjecture that in the setting of Theorem 7b it is T̃pp (G̃n ) ≤ log1+2q (n) + o(log n), without further restrictions on Gn , i.e. that push&pull cannot be slowed down informing almost all vertices. As a final remark note that Theorems 5 and 7 are tight in the sense that if an adversary may delete up to half of the edges at each vertex, then there are expander graphs that become disconnected. On those graphs a linear fraction of the vertices will remain uninformed forever. Outline The rest of this paper is structured as follows.
